newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to contest EU fowl rules, but not right now.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to contest EU fowl rules, but not right now.

text.p: Brazil intends to challenge European Union's import rules for chicken and turkey at the World Trade Organization, but such moves are not imminent, a Foreign Relations Ministry official said.
"We have taken the decision to ask for formal consultations but it's not something we're going to do today or tomorrow, more like by the end of the year," said the official who asked not to be named.

Brazil has long complained that it should be rewarded, not penalized, by EU's rules on chicken and turkey imports which allow fixed quotas of products from several non-member countries to enter the union at a zero-tariff.
The official said Brazil agreed to accept the scrapping in the early 1990s of a low import tariff for soybean products in return for an exclusive, low poultry tariff which never materialized.
An official with the EU's delegation said he had not received any formal warning from the Brazilian government that consultations were about to begin at the WTO.
